mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stop weakening and hold near current levels, discretionary trips to shops and restaurants will stabilize and edge up within four weeks. The mechanism fails if commuting remains depressed while retail also stays flat or falls.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stop declining or improve.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS falls below -10 percent after being less negative the prior week, outdoor substitution weakens and some visits shift back indoors to retail and dining within two weeks. The signal fails if PARKS rebounds or retail remains unchanged.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses below -10 after a weekly improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after PARKS drops below -10 and had improved in the prior weekly observation.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT creates more passing retail exposure and lunch-time errands, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. If only one of the two recovers, the effect should be weaker and may not appear.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over 28 days when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase together, or improves when only one proxy rises.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT of more than 3 points week-on-week signals tighter movement constraints or lower confidence, and retail visits then weaken within one week. If transit stabilizes, the retail effect should not materialize.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days after a week-on-week TRANSIT decline greater than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stays suppressed, more people stay close to home and shift spending to nearby essentials instead of discretionary retail, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks. The effect fails if residential intensity eases or workplaces recover materially.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above 7 and WORKPLACES stays below its current weekly level.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run improvement in GROCERY_PHARM after a prior dip indicates routine shopping is normalizing, which typically precedes a modest retail recovery within two weeks. The relationship breaks if grocery demand is rising because of precautionary stockpiling rather than routine activity.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns upward after a weekly decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM reverses upward from a prior weekly drop.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise together, leisure demand is being absorbed at home and outdoors rather than in commercial venues, so retail mobility falls over the next four weeks. If parks soften while residential remains high, the displacement should be weaker.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over 28 days when PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both increase from their current levels.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES improves for two consecutive weeks after a period of decline, it marks a durable easing in mobility constraints and retail visits should rise with a four-week lag. The signal fails when the workplace rebound is brief or immediately reverses.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks after declining
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last 28-day mean within 28 days after WORKPLACES posts two consecutive weekly gains.
